label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> when the fed-back input is "e" (sequence started with e), L>=6
explanation: Fires only at step t = L+1, the step right after <DEL>, where the model has just output original token 0 and gets it back as input, and only when that token is "e" (that is, the sequence starts with e). Activity there is near-certain when L >= 6 (dev P=0.999, R=0.98, F1=0.99). Magnitude grows strongly with sequence length: L=9 carries about 35% of the activation mass and L=6 only about 11%, with similar counts of active steps. At L=5 it fires only weakly and rarely (121 steps, 0.1% of mass), and it never fires for L<=4. It never fires during the original phase, at <DEL>, or at any other copy position, even when e is the input there. Rare tiny activations occur when g is fed back at the same position. It does not depend on which token comes next or on the rest of the sequence.

issues: The original predicate reproduces on the test split: precision 0.999, recall 0.980, F1 0.989, mass recall 0.999. The dev profile backs the main claims. Activations fire only in the copy phase and only at recall_idx==1. None fire in the original phase or at <DEL>. 99.9% of the mass has in_tok=e. Mass share by L is 0.1% (L=5), 11.2% (L=6), 23.7% (L=7), 30.0% (L=8) and 35.1% (L=9). Nothing fires for L<=4.
Removing the L>=6 condition gives dev precision 0.68, matching the reported number. Restricting to L==5 gives precision 0.045, so at L=5 the feature fires only weakly and rarely, as claimed.

Minor caveat: the test misses (230 steps, 0.1% of mass, all tiny at 0.01-0.08 of max) include a small pattern at L=9. The fed-back token there is b, 3 or g, and the second original token is e. So the claim that the feature 'does not depend on the other tokens' is very slightly off, and the 'g' activations seem tied to e at position 1. Other misses are weak activations at L=5 when the sequence starts with e. The test split has only 8 false positives, all at L=6. This is noise-level and not worth a new predicate.
